fields.description:
# Per-class fallback chains

## Context / Problem
A class may name a model that is not always reachable — a local endpoint that is down, a provider
being throttled. Today a single unreachable model fails the gate outright; there is no way to say
"use the local trivial model, but fall back to a hosted one".

## Approach
Consume the `fallback` array that the schema ticket already parses, constructing pydantic-ai's
`FallbackModel(default, *fallbacks, fallback_on=...)` per class. Fallback entries are INLINE model
configs (same shape as a slot), not references to named presets, so nothing requires the operator to
look up rebar vocabulary.

`fallback_on` must be set deliberately rather than left at its default. pydantic-ai's own docs warn
that provider SDK retry logic can delay failover substantially — a 429 may be retried inside the SDK
for up to ~60s before the fallback is ever reached — so the condition is narrowed to the errors where
switching providers actually helps (availability/rate-limit classes), not every exception.

**Alternative rejected — rebar-implemented retry/failover.** pydantic-ai already ships this and rebar
already depends on it; a second implementation would diverge from the runner's error taxonomy.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/` — construct `FallbackModel` from a class's fallback list where the model is built.
- `tests/unit/` — construction and selection tests.

## Testing
Unit tier with a stubbed model: no network, no live provider.
- a class with no `fallback` builds the plain model (no FallbackModel wrapper) — today's behaviour.
- a class with one fallback builds a FallbackModel whose default is the primary.
- an error in the configured `fallback_on` class selects the fallback.
- an error OUTSIDE that class propagates instead of silently failing over.

## DECIDED — the five runtime questions the first review blocked on

**1. `endpoint` on a fallback entry IS honored.** `resolve_fallback_chain` returns
`provider:model` STRINGS, which structurally cannot carry `endpoint` — so it is NOT the construction
input. It is retained only as the human-readable / provenance view. Construction consumes the full
`FallbackTarget` record (`model` + `provider` + `endpoint`) and builds each fallback through the SAME
provider-construction path as the primary. Dropping `endpoint` would silently ignore the main reason
to configure a fallback at all (a local OpenAI-compatible proxy backing a hosted primary).

**2 + 3. ONE `ProviderSession` builds the primary AND every fallback.** Not a session per entry.
`ProviderSession._closeables` is a plain list (`providers.py:102`) appended by each builder
(`providers.py:214`, `:276`) and drained by a single teardown loop (`providers.py:289`), so N
fallback clients registered on the same session are all closed exactly once when the run ends.
Constructing fallbacks outside the session — or in sessions of their own — leaks one
`httpx.AsyncClient` per Anthropic-typed fallback per call, which is a slow resource leak that no
functional test would catch. Each Anthropic-typed fallback still gets its OWN retrying transport via
`_build_retrying_anthropic_model`; sharing one transport across entries is NOT the fix.

**4. Capabilities are the CONSERVATIVE INTERSECTION over the whole candidate set.** With
`FallbackModel`, which model executes is unknown until runtime, so `capabilities_for`,
`cache_settings_for` and `_check_tool_capability` are computed over primary + every fallback and a
capability holds only if EVERY candidate has it. Concretely: a chain containing Bedrock
`claude-opus-4-8` (MEASURED `supports_temperature: False` — it rejects every value except the default)
withdraws `temperature` for the WHOLE chain. The alternative — compute from the primary and hope —
produces a run that succeeds or `ValidationException`s depending on which candidate answered, i.e. a
non-deterministic failure that reproduces only under provider degradation.

**Provenance records BOTH the candidate set and what actually ran.** `provider_provenance` gains the
ordered `candidates` (known at build time) and `ran_model` (resolved AFTER the call from the model
that answered). A verdict that records only the primary would ATTEST THE WRONG MODEL whenever a
fallback fired — which is exactly the misattribution story 343b exists to prevent, so the fallback
feature must not reintroduce it.

**5. `fallback_on` reuses the EXISTING failure taxonomy — it is not a new vocabulary.**
`failure.py` already classifies every provider error. Fall back on the classes where another provider
plausibly helps:

- `ResolutionClass.WAIT_AND_RETRY` — `ModelHTTPError` 429 (rate limit), 529, 500/502/503/504
- `ResolutionClass.CHANGE_PROVIDER_OR_MODEL`
- transport failures: `httpx.ConnectError`, `httpx.TimeoutException`, and `ModelAPIError`

Explicitly NOT falling back on:

- `CHANGE_SETTINGS` (401/403) — a credential/permission problem must fail LOUDLY. Silently shopping
  for a provider whose key happens to work converts a misconfiguration into a mystery bill.
- `CHANGE_INPUT` (400 context-length, 413) — another provider will not fix an oversized or malformed
  request; the SIZE LADDER already owns that path, and falling back would mask it.
- schema/validation failures — a structured-output mismatch is a rebar bug, not a provider outage.

Deriving `fallback_on` from `ResolutionClass` rather than an independent tuple means the two
classifications cannot drift, and a future taxonomy change updates both at once.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] a test asserts a class without `fallback` builds an unwrapped model (no behaviour change)
- [ ] a test asserts a class with `fallback` builds a FallbackModel whose default is the primary entry
- [ ] a test asserts an error in the configured condition selects the fallback entry
- [ ] a test asserts an error outside the condition PROPAGATES rather than failing over
- [ ] the chosen `fallback_on` condition is documented in-code with the SDK-retry caveat

- [ ] a test asserts a fallback entry carrying `endpoint` produces a model object built against THAT
      endpoint — not one silently built against the provider default
- [ ] a test asserts every fallback client is registered on the SAME `ProviderSession` and is closed
      on teardown: with N Anthropic-typed fallbacks, `_closeables` holds N+1 clients and all are
      closed exactly once (this fails against a per-entry-session implementation, which leaks)
- [ ] a test asserts a chain containing a model with `supports_temperature: False` withdraws
      `temperature` for the WHOLE chain, not just when that model is the primary
- [ ] a test asserts `provider_provenance` records the ordered `candidates` AND a `ran_model` equal
      to the model that actually answered — so a verdict produced by a fallback does not attest the
      primary
- [ ] a test asserts `fallback_on` fires on a 429/529/5xx and on a transport error, and does NOT
      fire on 401/403 or on a 400 context-length error (the loud-failure cases)
